newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary govt paper yields drop, further fall seen.
newsitem.headline: Hungary govt paper yields drop, further fall seen.

text.p: Yields on Hungary's government securities on the secondary market are likely to drop further this week following last week's declining trend, reflecting expectations of falling inflation, dealers said on Monday.
"The interest rate trend declined last week, and I do not see the end of this trend," said Bank Austria-Girocredit's Istvan Halasz. "(The market players) believe inflation is going down."
Hungary hopes to bring down year-on-year inflation to 20 percent by December from 28.3 percent in December 1995.
Dealers said that most government bond and treasury bill yields dropped by 0.1 to 0.2 percent last week.

Papers one month ahead of maturity were sold at a yield of 22.37 percent on the secondary market, while at six months the yield was 22.75 to 22.8 percent and for bonds one and two years ahead of maturity the yield was 22.85 percent, though there were no sellers for two-year papers, dealers said. @

They said the National Bank of Hungary's move to cut most of its repo rates by 0.25 percent last week and low levels of overnight interest rates on the interbank market in the last days of the previous reserve period also contributed to a last week's drop in yields.
Strong demand for six- and twelve-month Treasury bills at last week's auctions and lower-than-expected average yields set at the auctions also helped the yields to fall, they added.
Dealers said the yields on the secondary market are likely to drop further by a few tenths of a percentage point this week.
The auction of the two-year 1998/K series government bond on Thursday may have a crucial impact on the market, they added.
Most dealers expected strong demand at the auction and the yield to drop by 0.17 to 0.47 percentage points from 22.85 percent set at an auction on October 24.
